reassurance_anchor.text_en: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.

verses.translation_en: Do not despair of the mercy of Allah.

socratic_dropdowns.question: Who is this verse addressed to?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It is addressed to those who have transgressed against themselves. It is a call to return.

evidence.arabic: قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ
evidence.translation_en: Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves.'
evidence.why_cited: It names those who went too far, not the perfect.

evidence.translation_en: Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
evidence.why_cited: It names forgiveness and mercy as His attributes.

verses.translation_en: For indeed, with hardship comes ease.

socratic_dropdowns.question: Why 'with' and not 'after'?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: The Quran uses 'with'. Ease is placed with hardship. They are intertwined.

evidence.translation_en: For indeed, with hardship comes ease.

evidence.arabic: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا
evidence.translation_en: And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair.
evidence.why_cited: It places ease as a promise tied to taqwa.

verses.translation_en: And do not despair of the relief of Allah.

socratic_dropdowns.question: Who said this?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: Yaqub, to his sons. He had lost Yusuf. Years had passed. And yet, his words were hope.

evidence.arabic: إِنَّمَا أَشْكُو بَثِّي وَحُزْنِي إِلَى اللَّهِ
evidence.translation_en: I only complain of my suffering and my grief to Allah.
evidence.why_cited: It shows grief spoken, but not without hope.

evidence.translation_en: And do not despair of the relief of Allah.
evidence.why_cited: It commands hope after long grief.

verses.arabic_text: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مَخْرَجًا
verses.translation_en: And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What is the way out?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It is not described. It is left open. The verse promises a way, not the shape of it.

evidence.arabic: وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مَخْرَجًا
evidence.translation_en: And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out.
evidence.why_cited: It promises a way out without describing it.

evidence.translation_en: And will provide for him from where he does not expect.
evidence.why_cited: It adds provision from unexpected places.

verses.translation_en: Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.

socratic_dropdowns.question: What is the context of this verse?
socratic_dropdowns.answer: It comes after a description of tests. The verse answers the question: when will help come?

evidence.arabic: أَمْ حَسِبْتُمْ أَن تَدْخُلُوا الْجَنَّةَ وَلَمَّا يَأْتِكُم مَّثَلُ الَّذِينَ خَلَوْا مِن قَبْلِكُم
evidence.translation_en: Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while such testing has not yet come to you?
evidence.why_cited: It names the test before the promise.

evidence.translation_en: Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.
evidence.why_cited: It answers the question of timing.
